title: auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Intermittent 401 + 429 errors observed for hosted API (mostly prod, occasional staging) starting 2026-03-05 18:30 UTC. Reports from 3 customers (small spike) + internal synthetic monitors. Impact: short-lived failures (~30s-2m) causing retries and some downstream errors in callers.

Observed patterns:
- 401s tend to cluster around the same minute as 429 bursts in some traces (not always).
- 401 payloads returned to clients: {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"Invalid API key"} or plain 401 with empty body.
- 429 responses include headers in some cases: Retry-After: 3, X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: <unix-ts>.
- Synthetic monitor (eu-prod-synth1) showed 401s at 2026-03-05T18:31:02Z and 18:31:04Z then recovered.

Commands / repro attempts:
1) Basic request with good key (worked):
   curl -i -X POST 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate' \n     -H 'Authorization: Bearer $GOOD_KEY' \n     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n     -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}'

   -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK

2) Using an obviously bad key (repro 401):
   curl -i -X POST 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate' \n     -H 'Authorization: Bearer BAD_KEY' \n     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n     -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}'

   -> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
   Body: {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"Invalid API key"}

3) When we saw 401s in prod, I pulled headers from failing requests (via proxy logs):
   - Host: api.redwood.com
   - Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
   - request-id: 01FJ3X...
   - user-agent: curl/7.82

4) 429 reproduction (rate limit header present):
   - Spammed endpoint from loadgen -> got 429 with Retry-After=2 and X-RateLimit-Remaining=0.

Server-side log excerpts (sanitized):
- 2026-03-05T18:31:02Z host=api-route-3 req_id=01FJ3X user_id=acct_123 api_key_id=key_abc status=401 reason=invalid_signature
- 2026-03-05T18:31:02Z host=ratelimiter-1 req_id=01FJ3X api_key_id=key_abc limit=1000 remain=0 reset=1700000000 status=429
- 2026-03-05T18:31:04Z host=auth-proxy req_id=01FJ3Y api_key_id=key_def cache_hit=false oauth_state=unknown status=401

Initial observations / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Partial key rotation churn (some service updated key store earlier) -> transient invalid_signature / invalid_key between services (auth-proxy vs kv-store) -> 401s.
  - Evidence: some 401 logs show reason=invalid_signature and api_key_id present. Also saw a deployment of key-sync-job ~18:30.
- Hypothesis B: Rate limiter mis-attribution where when a key hits global limit, some path incorrectly returns 401 instead of 429 (bug in error translation or middleware).
  - Evidence: 429 entries appear for same req_id close in time; some proxies downstream return 401 for clients even though ratelimiter emitted 429.
- Hypothesis C: Edge / CDN caching edge-case: stale cached 401 responses returned for certain Authorization header patterns (unlikely but possible).
- Hypothesis D: Client-side: some clients sending truncated Authorization header due to proxy (rare).

Things I've tried / checked so far:
- Checked key-sync job logs around 18:28-18:34 -> one run completed with a warning about a TTL refresh; rollout to 2 nodes delayed 20s. (suspicious)
- Verified API key metadata in account service for key_abc/key_def -> active, not revoked, usage within quota.
- Queried rate-limiter metrics -> small spike at 18:31 but within expected for minute window; per-key metrics show key_abc hit limit then dropped back.
- Correlated request-ids across auth proxy and gateway -> found sequences where gateway logged 429 then auth-proxy logged 401 for same req_id (translation mismatch).
- Looked at proxy code that maps limiter error -> translation layer returns 401 for some error codes (open PR in 2026-02 but not released?).

Immediate next steps (TODO):
- [ ] Confirm which commit was deployed to auth-proxy and gateway around 18:28-18:32 (ask infra/release). + Michael to check.
- [ ] Reproduce locally with same key sync cadence: run key-sync job and issue requests concurrently to see race (I have a small test harness).
- [ ] Add extra logging at translation boundary to capture original limiter error & final response code (hotfix if possible).
- [ ] Temporarily increase rate-limiter per-key throttle for affected accounts (mitigation) -> needs SRE approval.
- [ ] Check CDN/edge caches for any caching rules keyed on Authorization header (unlikely, but check config).
- [ ] Contact customers affected with short postmortem once root cause nailed.

Short-term mitigations tried/planned:
- Throttle smoothing: configure gateway to prefer 429 semantics consistently and not normalize to 401. (config patch queued)
- Roll back recent auth-proxy change if we reproduce correlation with the key-sync timing.

Notes for postmortem / debugging breadcrumbs to capture later:
- Timeline of deploys and key-sync runs mapped to 1s resolution.
- Full chain trace for example req_id that exhibited 429->401.
- Copy of rate-limiter config & recent PRs modifying error codes mapping.
- Any rollback of CDN config in last week.

Links / refs:
- Jira INF-2345 (investigate 401/429 translation bug)
- Slack thread: #prod-issues thread from 2026-03-05 (link above)
- Key-sync job: infra repo, job id key-sync-v2 (recent deploy 2026-03-05 18:27)

Scratchy hypotheses summary (for later):
- Most likely: race between key-store refresh and auth-proxy reads causing transient invalid_signature -> 401s.
- Also likely: translation bug where ratelimiter errors get mapped to 401 in some code paths.

Owner / next owner: Lena (me). Michael helping with deploy logs. Aisha to check customer impact comms.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc lightweight; move final timeline + evidence to Jira ticket INF-2345 when we have a root cause.
